name: dkdv_lsefence
idea: Stop the loop-carried lse copy (v_mov V650<-V693) from being hoisted to right after lse's last use at Vaddr 17104, where it forces s_wait_loadcnt 0x23 on this iteration's own prefetch (issued about 460 cycles earlier). Pin it into the tail region instead, below the dK/dV WMMA fence, where the loop's existing s_wait_loadcnt 0x0 (19448) has already drained it.
change_spec: Copy arms/r29 to arms/dkdv_lsefence. In kernels.py _dkdv_impl._body (L355-513): insert `rocdl.sched_barrier(0)` right after the b_do/b_q construction loop (the `for dtile in range_constexpr(NDO): ... b_q.append(...)` block that starts at `b_do = []` L476), just before `new = [None] * (2 * NKV * NDO)` (L482). Nothing else changes. Why this works: the PHI-elimination COPYs for the carried `nxt` (4 lse/delta b32 plus 32 b128, returned at L512) sit at the end of the single-block loop body (.LBB0_11). A full sched_barrier stops the machine scheduler from raising them above the fence. SIInsertWaitcnts then puts their loadcnt wait in the tail, where the 0x0 at 19448 already covers it. The values are unchanged, so dK/dV are bitwise identical to r29. Gate (compile-only, free): in 21_final_isa.s the `v_mov_b32 ... v693`-class lse/delta copies must appear after the first dK/dV WMMA; there must be no s_wait_loadcnt with a threshold above 0x10 between the S/dP WMMAs and phase K; VGPR at most 729+8, 0 spill. Then ATT: phase H (Vaddr ~17140) should drop from 133.9 cycles/iter (notes/dkdv_loop_wall.txt:183) to under 10, and the iteration-time spread should collapse (p90 2029 -> ~1650).
evidence: notes/dkdv_loop_wall.txt:183: the s_wait_loadcnt 0x23 at 17140 costs 133.9 cycles of 1714.9 per iteration (7.8%). dispatch_10 csv L1600-1601: the wait sits immediately before `v_mov_b32 v138/*v650*/, v181/*v693*/`. 29.4% of iterations (1111 of 3780) stall more than 100 cycles, 434 on average, and this is the whole of the p90-p10 spread. The hh=1 lse copy and the delta copies are placed later and stall only 2-3 cycles (0x22 at 17624, 0x20 at 18888), which shows the load itself lands in time once the copy is late enough. Gain: 134 x 0.8 ≈ 107 cycles/iter = 6.2% of k_dkdv; k_dkdv is 63.5% of bwd cycles (7.26e6/11.44e6, roofline REPORT) -> ~4% of total bwd.
vgpr_risk: Low. Live ranges do not grow: the carried lse regs already live to the back-edge, and V693 now lives about 1700 cycles longer, which costs 4-8 VGPR at most. Headroom is 729 -> 1024 (1 wave/SIMD either way).
bounds_risk: None. No index or address expression changes; the same loads and values are used.
closed_axis_conflict: Looks like #24 (source reorder, ISA identical) and #8 (sched_barrier/sched_group_barrier losses), but it differs. This is a single full fence that pins a register copy, not a VALU/MFMA interleave recipe. sched_barrier(0) is the proven order-pinning tool in this file (g51, L300). It also does not change prefetch depth or ordering (#2/#6, g27): the loads still issue at the same place with the same FIFO order, and only the COPY's wait moves.

name: dkdv_trorder
idea: Reorder the final DS phase so the first dK/dV WMMA waits for about 25 DS ops instead of 57. Issue a_p(kh0) and b_do first, then a_ds(kh0) and b_q, then kh1's A operands. Use sched_barrier(0) fences so each WMMA group is in the same scheduling region as the loads the next group needs, and s_wait_dscnt stays partial (ASM style: loads one phase ahead, never waiting for 0).
change_spec:
Copy arms/r29 to arms/dkdv_trorder. In _body replace L476-507 (b_do/b_q loop plus the kh WMMA loop) with an explicit 4-region emission (`tr`, the column math and the WMMA calls are unchanged; only the order and the fences are new):
```
rocdl.sched_barrier(0)                       # F0: all P/dS + Q/dO stores above
col0 = lane_c*2 + 0
a_p0 = tr(lds_p + lane_r*S_ROW_B + col0, S_ROW_B)
b_do = [tr(lds_do + lane_r*X_ROW_B + (lane_c+dtile*16)*2, X_ROW_B) for dtile in range(NDO)]
rocdl.sched_barrier(0)                       # F1
a_ds0 = tr(lds_ds + ... col0 ...)
b_q = [tr(lds_q + ...) for dtile]            # region 2: loads + 8 dV WMMA (a_p0 x b_do)
for dtile: new[0*NDO+dtile] = wmma(a_p0, b_do[dtile], acc[...], reuseA=dtile>0)
rocdl.sched_barrier(0)                       # F2
col1 = lane_c*2 + 32
a_p1 = tr(lds_p ... col1); a_ds1 = tr(lds_ds ... col1)   # region 3: + 8 dK WMMA kh0
for dtile: new[(NKV+0)*NDO+dtile] = wmma(a_ds0, b_q[dtile], ...)
rocdl.sched_barrier(0)                       # F3
for dtile: new[1*NDO+dtile] = wmma(a_p1, b_do[dtile], ...)
for dtile: new[(NKV+1)*NDO+dtile] = wmma(a_ds1, b_q[dtile], ...)
```
The accumulator order per acc slot is unchanged, so this is bitwise. Variant b drops F3 (lets the kh1 loads float). Gate (free, ISA): the first dK/dV WMMA must be preceded by s_wait_dscnt with a threshold of at least 0x10 (today 0x6 after 57 ops, ISA:1868); no s_wait_dscnt 0x0 before the 17th tail WMMA; VGPR at most 740, 0 spill. ATT target: `L` (notes/dkdv_loop_wall.txt:394-398) 199 -> <=70 cycles/iter. Note: F0 also pins the carried copies below it, so this arm subsumes dkdv_lsefence. Measure alone, then stack.
evidence: REPORT dkdv §2: s_wait_dscnt 0x6 at 18872 costs 188.0 cycles/iter (WALL:394), plus 10.7 and 1.9. It waits for 23 stores + 34 of 40 tr loads (~29 KB) because a_p/a_ds are issued LAST and DS completes in order. Stores back-pressure to 3-4.6 cycles each after the 12th (WALL:341-353). New order: the first WMMA needs 23 st + 18 ld = 41 ops (and 7 st + 18 ld = 25 when stacked with dkdv_qdoburst); later regions' loads are at least 8 WMMA (64 cycles) ahead of use. ASM does 2 DS per WMMA gap at 8.1 cycles/gap with 68 cycles/step total dscnt (REPORT asm §7). Estimate: 199 -> ~80 cycles, i.e. ~120 cycles/iter = 7% of k_dkdv -> ~4.4% of bwd. Taking 3.5% for overlap with lsefence.
vgpr_risk: Low to medium. b_q (64 VGPR) is now loaded after the first 8 WMMA issue rather than before, which lowers peak pressure slightly. The fences can stop the allocator from overlapping the rotation copies with b_q; check that VGPR stays at or below 760.
bounds_risk: None. The LDS addresses are the same expressions as today (tr/col), with no new global index.
closed_axis_conflict: Relates to #12 (reopened: 'order has to be fixed in the source, because hints do not work'), #9 (g93 double-buffered rings ignored by LLVM) and #24 (source reorder produced identical ISA). The difference is that this uses sched_barrier(0) full fences, which DO change ISA order (g51 proof at L300), instead of relying on source order or ring structure. g95 (-3.1%) moved P/dS across the back-edge, which is a different mechanism. No change to the WMMA chain split (#20) or operand reuse (#19).

name: dkdv_qdoburst
idea: Emit all 32 Q/dO staging ds_stores (both hh halves) as one burst at the top of the body, fenced. Today the compiler scatters them: 7 in phase C, 4 in E, 6 in F, and the 16 hh=1 stores are sunk into the critical final DS drain. The burst removes 2 of the 5 mid-body DS<->WMMA switch pairs and takes 16 stores out of the dscnt 0x6 critical path.
change_spec: Copy arms/r29 to arms/dkdv_qdoburst. In _body (L355): split the `for hh in range_constexpr(2):` loop at L383 in two. (1) A new first loop over hh that ONLY does the ds_store pairs (the current L386-396 store block, using the same xo/o/dp/qp expressions) and builds qfr/dfr into per-hh lists. (2) Immediately after it, `rocdl.sched_barrier(0)`. (3) The existing hh loop from `q_glob = ...` onward (S/dP WMMA, softmax, P/dS stores) reads qfr[hh]/dfr[hh] from those lists. Keep `nxt = _ldqd(qt_n, gh_n)` where it is, BEFORE the store burst, so the 4 lse/delta b32 stay at the FIFO head (g48/g51 rule). The b128 loads may then sit above the burst, which is fine. Variant b: put the store burst BEFORE `nxt = _ldqd(...)`, so the stores overlap VMEM latency, and check the loadcnt thresholds stay partial. Bitwise identical. Gate (free, ISA): one contiguous group of at least 32 ds_store_b128 before the first S/dP WMMA; the final pre-dK/dV DS group has 7 stores (not 23); VGPR at most 740, 0 spill. ATT target: phases C+E+F store/switch ~161 -> ~110, K 123.5 -> ~70.
evidence: REPORT dkdv §1b: mid-body Q/dO stores plus DS<->WMMA switches ≈ 161 cycles/iter (switch gaps 25.8 WALL:54, 21+24.7 WALL:112,116, 27+25.5 WALL:151,157). Phase K has 16 delayed hh=1 stores in its 23 (ISA order at 18360-18860). A 32-store burst issues at about 12x1 + 20x4 ≈ 92 cycles plus one ~26-cycle DS->WMMA switch, versus 161 + ~70 today. Net ≈ 100-110 cycles/iter ≈ 6% of k_dkdv. Some of it overlaps with dkdv_trorder's gain on phase L, so ~2.5% of bwd standalone.
vgpr_risk: Low. The Q/dO carried regs (pre[4:]) are already live from the loop head to the S/dP WMMAs; the burst only moves their last DS read earlier. qfr/dfr shuffles are register-level (no new regs if coalesced). Worst case +16 VGPR.
bounds_risk: None. Same LDS offsets (xo + dt*64 + u*32), no global address change.
closed_axis_conflict: Not #13 (the P1 probe deleted the Q/dO LDS round trip: -6.98%). This keeps the round trip and only groups the stores. Not #8 (it uses no sched_group_barrier interleave recipe, only one full fence). Relates to #12 (reopened switch cost, 29 cycles/switch per the roofline REPORT) by cutting the switch count from 7 to about 5.

name: dkdv_divfree
idea: Replace the two runtime integer divisions per iteration (qi = ii // G and qj = jj // G, where G is a runtime Int32 kernel arg) with a shift and a mask. The SALU udiv expansion is phase A, 46 cycles/iter plus part of the address setup.
change_spec: Copy arms/r29 to arms/dkdv_divfree. In _dkdv_impl, in the prologue before the loop definitions (~L330, next to nqt2), compute a wave-uniform `lgG` from the runtime G with a select chain: `lgG = (G==2).select(1, (G==4).select(2, (G==8).select(3, (G==16).select(4, (G==32).select(5, 0)))))`, and `mG = G - 1`. In qloop_full (L527-545), qloop_mask (L518-524) and qloop_full2/_tail (L555-580): replace `qi = ii // G` with `qi = ii >> lgG` (fx shift on Int32; if FlyDSL lacks `>>`, use arith.shrui through fx.as_ir_value), and `ii - qi*G` with `ii & mG`. Do the same for qj/jj and for q1/i1 in qloop_full2. In impl.py launch_dkdv caller, add a host assert that G is a power of two in {1,2,4,8,16,32}. If it is not, keep the old kernel by passing a constexpr flag DIVFREE=False. Values are identical, so the output is bitwise. Gate (free, ISA): no v_cvt_f32_u32/v_rcp_iflag/s_mul_hi udiv sequence in .LBB0_11; loop SALU count at 15628-15748 drops from ~20 to about 4.
evidence: REPORT dkdv §1a phase A: 'Loop index math in SALU (qi=ii//G, qj=jj//G, SRC:531,539)' = 46.0 cycles/iter (Vaddr 15628-15748) of 1714.9. The report also counts part of phase B's 53.2 as dependent VALU address math, with VALU->VMEM address dependencies of 16/17 cycles (WALL:38,76). kernels.py L170 shows G is a runtime argument, so LLVM cannot strength-reduce the division. Expected ~40 cycles/iter = 2.3% of k_dkdv -> ~1.5% of bwd.
vgpr_risk: None. The change is SGPR-only (lgG and mG are wave-uniform).
bounds_risk: Must prove on the CPU that for every G in {1,2,4,8,16,32} and every ii in [0, n), (ii>>lgG, ii&mG) == (ii//G, ii%G). This is trivial, but run it in the CPU proof script, including the jj clamp path where jj = n-1. For G not a power of two the host must route to the old path.
closed_axis_conflict: Resembles #21 (g92 constant hoist, 0.9662) and #3 (unroll). It differs because g92 hoisted constants, whereas this removes a ~40-cycle serial SALU dependency chain that feeds the VMEM addresses. No fence or order change.

It targets the largest single tail cost, the rotation v_mov_b64 plus WAR v_nop at 192.5 cycles/iter. The previous verdict (+6.5-7.3% loss) came from B0 before the reflash, where the analogous k_dq u2n result has since reversed sign.
change_spec: Copy arms/r29 to arms/dkdv_ku2. In kernels.py set `KV_U2 = True` (L55). qloop_full2 (L555-580) and qloop_tail already exist and are bitwise-identical by construction (comment at L548-553). Gate (free, ISA): 0 v_mov_b64 in the loop, VGPR at most 740 (lab-kdq reported 644), 0 spill. Then run the standard tools/arm.sh at prod AND capture ATT for k_dkdv. Stack variant ku2+lsefence+trorder: put the fences from dkdv_trorder in both bodies of qloop_full2; the second body's F0 also keeps its prefetch copies late. Decision rule: keep if prod >= +0.5%, otherwise record the ATT phase deltas (M should drop from 432.5 to ~260 cycles per body).
evidence: REPORT dkdv §3.6 / §1b: phase M = 30 dK/dV WMMAs with 64 v_mov_b64 + 51 v_nop = 432.5 cycles, 192.5 above the 8-cycle floor (11.2% of k_dkdv; WALL:410-548). 16 tail WMMAs are 20-22 cycles apart instead of 8 because of WAR on B operands. lab-kdq/REPORT.md:30 says ku2 was +7.3% slower on B0 pre-reflash with no ATT. levers #22: u2n was -3.06% on B0 but +3.3% on A0 (0928__a0_repro/REPORT.md:176-182), so B0 unroll verdicts do not transfer. Upper bound 192/1715 x 63.5% = 7.1% of bwd; expected ~2% given the history.
vgpr_risk: Low. lab-kdq measured 729 -> 644 VGPR. The risk is code size or I-cache (two bodies of ~550 instructions each).
bounds_risk: None new. qloop_full2 already clamps jj; the odd tail goes to qloop_tail. Re-run the existing CPU iteration-coverage proof for n odd and even.
closed_axis_conflict: Directly reopens #21 (ku2 op +6.5%, CM). The justification is new evidence: A0 reversed the B0 unroll verdict for k_dq (#22 RE), and the ATT now attributes 192.5 cycles/iter to the exact mechanism ku2 removes. Differs from #3 (h60/g72 unroll to remove the loop-head drain), which targeted the drain rather than the rotation copies.

name: dqg_earlyclump
idea: In k_dqg's U2 loop, move body 2's K/V prefetch clump (32 buffer_load_b128 for block ii+2) from the end of the trip (cum ~2890-3314, lead only 214-490 cycles to its consumer, s_wait_loadcnt 0x20) to right after body 2's S/dP WMMAs, the point where the carried K/V set dies. It stays a single clump, and the register lifetime is unchanged. Variant c also folds the column offsets into buffer immediate/soffset to kill the xcnt waits.
change_spec: Copy arms/r29 to arms/dqg_earlyclump. In _dqg_impl._body (L1277-1353) add a parameter `pf_mid=False`. When `carry and pf_mid`: do NOT call `nxt = _ldkv(kv0_n)` at L1279. Instead, after the `for kt in range_constexpr(NKT)` S/dP+softmax loop and before `a_ds = [...]` (L1335), emit `rocdl.sched_barrier(0); nxt = _ldkv(kv0_n); rocdl.sched_barrier(0)` (variant a: both fences; variant b: only the first fence, which lets the clump sink but not rise). In kvloop_full's DQ_PF and DQ_U2 branch (~L1361-1375), pass `pf_mid=True` only for the SECOND _body call; body 1 keeps its head clump, which already has a 1400-2900 cycle lead. Variant c (stack after a/b): in gfrag2 (L1230-1233) build the address as a loop-invariant lane VGPR voff = ((row)*rs_kv + half)*16 bytes, plus a wave-uniform SGPR soffset = (base_kv + (kv0+kt*16)*rs_kv)*16, plus an immediate (dt*64 [+32]). Emit via rocdl.raw_ptr_buffer_load(res, rsrc, voff, soff, aux) (~/.local/flydsl032/flydsl/expr/rocdl/__init__.py:791), taking rsrc from the same make_buffer_tensor as g_k/g_v. Bitwise identical. Gates (free, ISA): (a/b) the tail clump now starts before the first dQ WMMA of body 2, and the instruction distance from the last clump buffer_load to `s_wait_loadcnt 0x20` exceeds ~60% of the trip (lead at least 1000 cycles by CSV latency sum); VGPR at most 1024, 0 spill, 0 scratch. (c) 0 s_wait_xcnt and at most 2 v_or_b32 in the loop (today xcnt at ISA:654-658). ATT: loadcnt 0x20 at Vaddr 11344 should drop from 302 to under 60 wall cycles/trip, and the slow-wave excess (+613/trip on wv0/4/8/12) should shrink.
evidence: REPORT dqg §2: s_wait_loadcnt 0x20 (FQcsv L670, Vaddr 11344) = 302 wall cycles/trip of 3576 (7.8% of k_dqg), 431 on slow waves. It waits on the tail clump 18676-19440 whose lead is 214-490 cycles, while the head-clump waits never stall with a lead of 1400-2900. Body 2's last carried-set consumer is at cum ~2233, versus the clump at ~2890-3314, so moving it gains ~700-1000 cycles of lead. xcnt 0x2/0x1/0x0 = 109+7.6+4.3 = ~121 cycles/trip (3.2%) from v_or 0xc0/0xe0 address rebuilds at 11132-11156. k_dqg = 35% of bwd (4.00e6/11.44e6). (a/b): ~250 cycles/trip = 7% of k_dqg ≈ 2.4% of bwd; (c) adds ~1.2%.
vgpr_risk: Medium. k_dqg is at 991/1024 VGPR. If the fences stop the clump from being allocated onto the dead carried set, VGPR rises by up to 128 and spills. Hard gate: 0 spill; if it fails, try variant b (single upper fence). Variant c reduces VGPR (fewer address regs).
bounds_risk: (a/b): none, since the same _ldkv(jj*KV_STEP) with the existing jj clamp is used. (c) changes the address expression: CPU-prove that voff + soff + imm == old t*16 for all (kv0, kt, row, half, dt) at every validated shape, that soff stays below num_records (the buffer's true extent still clamps OOB to 0), and that soff is wave-uniform (kv0 is uniform).
closed_axis_conflict: Not #4 (g63, prefetch depth 1->2, -19.33%): depth stays 1. Not #5 (g66, spreading the loads, -21.9%) or h37: the loads stay one contiguous clump, as h37 recommends. Not #6 (move prefetch after barrier-2 in the 4-wave S1): that was a multi-wave barrier placement. Relies on #22 (reopened U2) staying the shipped k_dqg form; if the r20-style k_dq wins its A0 A/B, port the same idea there.

name: dkdv_flip
idea: Switch to the ASM GEMM direction inside the 1-wave k_dkdv: compute S = Q*K^T and dP = dO*V^T (M=q, N=kv), so each lane's S/dP accumulator holds a fixed kv column (lane%16) and 8 q rows (hh*16+half*8+si). Concatenating hh=0 and hh=1 gives exactly the 16x32 B-fragment of dV^T = dO^T*P and dK^T = Q^T*dS (K = 32 q). P and dS then go straight from the C registers through cvt_pk into the B operand, and the P/dS LDS round trip disappears: 8 ds_store, 8 tr16 loads, the P-store switches, and the in-order drain behind the `s_wait_dscnt 0x6`. This is also the enabler for the TDM, 2-wave and 4-wave arms below.
change_spec:
Copy arms/r29 to arms/dkdv_flip. Edit kernels.py `_dkdv_impl` only; k_dqg is untouched.
(1) S/dP WMMA (~L406-415): swap the operands to `s_acc = wmma(v8f, _ir(qfr[dt]), _ir(kf[kh][dt]), s_acc)` and `p_acc = wmma(v8f, _ir(dfr[dt]), _ir(vf[kh][dt]), p_acc)`. The A and B fragment layouts on gfx1250 16x16x32 are symmetric (lane%16 = row/col, elements along K), so kf/vf/qfr/dfr are reused byte for byte.
(2) LSE/delta become per element. In `_ldqd` (L273-308), replace the 4 scalar `_ldv(g_lse/g_del, base_l+qg, Float32, 1)` loads with 2 vec4 loads per (hh, tensor): `_ldv(g_lse4, (base_l + q0 + hh*16 + half*8)//4 + u, Float32, 4)` for u = 0,1, with `g_lse4 = _bv(LSE, nl_b, fx.Float32, 4)`, and the same for g_del4. That is 8 buffer_load_b128 instead of 4 b32. Keep the `sched_barrier(0)` head-of-FIFO placement. In `_body`, set `lse_q[si] = pre[hh*4 + (si//4)][si%4]` and `del_q` likewise, and use per-element `(masked[si] - lse_q[si])` and `(pv_[si] - del_q[si])` (packed pk_add still applies).
(3) Causal mask, masked body only (~L424-436): kv = kv0 + kh*16 + row and q = q0 + hh*16 + half*8 + si; predicate `(kv > q + cshift) & causal`.
(4) Delete the P/dS LDS stores (`off=`... two `llvm_dialect.store` to lds_p/lds_ds, ~L446-454). Instead keep `p_bf[hh][kh]` and `ds_bf[hh][kh]` as v8 bf16 values, and after both hh build `bP[kh] = p_bf[0][kh].shuffle(p_bf[1][kh], range(16))` and `bdS[kh]` the same way.
(5) Output GEMM (~L474-503): keep `b_do`/`b_q` from `tr(lds_do/lds_q ...)` unchanged; they are now the A operands (lane%16 = d, elements along q). Delete a_p/a_ds. Emit, for kh in NKV and dtile in NDO: `new[kh*NDO+dtile] = wmma(v8f, _ir(b_do[dtile]), _ir(bP[kh]), acc[...], reuseA=False, reuseB=(dtile>0))`, and the same with b_q/bdS for dK^T. Issue b_do[0], b_q[0] first in source.
(6) Epilogue: the accumulator tile (kh, dtile) now holds dV^T with lane%16 = kv row and half*8+si = 8 consecutive d. Replace the g86 LDS-staged bf16 epilogue (~L648-708) with direct stores: `_stv([ov[si].to(bf16) for si in 8], g_dv8, (base_kv + (kv0+kh*16+row)*rs_kv) + dtile*2 + half, BFloat16)`, which is 16 buffer_store_b128 per tensor. The PARTIAL fp32 path (~L637-646) gets the same index change with 2 vec4 fp32 stores per tile.
(7) LDS: drop the lds_p/lds_ds rings. The allocation becomes 2*32*X_ROW_B = 17408 B; keep 70656 only if a 4-WG rung is needed, since occupancy is VGPR-bound anyway.
(8) impl.py: when Sq % 8 != 0, dispatch the r29 k_dkdv; the vec4 LSE path requires Sq % 8 == 0.
Gate: compile-only 0 spill, loop ISA shows 0 ds_store of P/dS and 32 ds_load_tr16 (was 40); then ATT the loop and check that the dscnt wait before the first dV WMMA falls from 188 cycles/iteration.
evidence: dkdv ATT (notes/dkdv_loop_wall.txt): `s_wait_dscnt 0x6/0x2/0x0` = 199 cycles/iteration (WALL:394,398; CSV:1857). It waits on 23 stores + 34 loads because a_p/a_ds are issued last, and 7 of those stores plus 8 of those loads are the P/dS round trip. The P-store switches in phase F cost about 50 cycles (WALL:151,157), and the phase-K store back-pressure 3-4.6 cycles/op (WALL:341-353). Removing 8 st + 8 ld plus the a_p dependence leaves the first dV WMMA waiting on about 18 DS ops instead of 57: about 130 cycles from the dscnt wait, about 50 from switches, about 30 from DS issue. That is roughly 210 of 1715 cycles, about 12% of k_dkdv. k_dkdv is 63% of bwd cycles (PMC 7.26e6 of 11.44e6), so about 7.5% of bwd; I discount to 6% for LLVM reordering. ASM section 11 of the asm report confirms the design: P/dS never touch LDS.
vgpr_risk: Low to moderate. Expect 729 -> about 760: +32 VGPR for P/dS bf16 held until the dV GEMM, +24 for per-element LSE/delta (current and carried), -32 for the a_p/a_ds tr16 results. That is well under 1024 and stays at 1 wave/SIMD. Check for spills at the compile gate.
bounds_risk: Changes these index expressions: the LSE/delta load (vec4 at (base_l+q0+hh*16+half*8)//4; needs Sq%8==0, host-guarded), the causal predicate (kv/q roles swapped), and the dK/dV epilogue store index (row = kv, 8 d per lane). CPU proof needed: extend lab3/bounds_proof.py to the vec4 LSE index (max < nl_b/16 vec4 units) and the new epilogue index (max = size-8, 16-B aligned) on prod, proxy, fast (nsp=1/2/16) and the UT Sq!=Skv shapes. Loads still clamp through _clampqt.
closed_axis_conflict: Resembles #12/g95 (P/dS carried across the back edge, -3.1%) and #13 (Q/dO LDS round trip, P1 -6.98%), but differs from both. g95 kept the LDS round trip and only moved it. name: dkdv_flip_tdm
idea: On top of dkdv_flip, move Q/dO onto the ASM data path. Q and dO tiles for iteration i+1 (and i+2) are brought into a 2-deep padded LDS ring by TDM (tensor_load_2d, tensorcnt). The S/dP A operands are read from LDS with plain ds_load_b128, one hh ahead of use. The dV^T/dK^T A operands are read with tr16 as now. This removes the dual-use VGPR staging (32 buffer_load_b128, 32 ds_store per iteration), the 128-VGPR carried prefetch with its 64 back-edge v_mov_b64 and WAR v_nops, and the VALU address math.
change_spec:
Copy arms/dkdv_flip to arms/dkdv_flip_tdm.
(1) Import aiter's shim exactly as in output/0925__flydsl/tdm-screen/tdm_screen.py:22-24 (`tdm_ops_gfx1250`: make_tensor_descriptor_2d, tensor_load_2d, tensor_wait). FlyDSL 0.3.2's own tdm_ops cannot take a Fly shared view.
(2) LDS layout: ring slots r = 0,1, each holding [Q 32x272 B | dO 32x272 B] = 17408 B, so the ring is 34816 B total. The descriptor for a tensor: global ptr Q (or DO), tensor_shape = (B*Sq, Hq*D) with TRUE extents, strides (Hq*D, 1), tile (32 rows, 128 cols) at global_offset (bat*Sq + qt*32, qh*D), elem_bytes 2, LDS row pad 16 B (h47-49 showed pad works when set explicitly).
(3) `_ldqd(qt, gh)` becomes `_tdm_issue(slot, qt, gh)`: 2 tensor_load_2d (Q, dO) plus the flip arm's 8 vec4 LSE/delta buffer loads (these stay VGPR-carried, 32 VGPR; g56 showed the async-LDS path for LSE/delta lost 6.84%). qloop_full carries only acc + LSE/delta + slot parity. In `_body`, issue TDM for iteration i+2 into slot (i%2) only after that slot's last reader (the dK^T tr16 of iteration i). Wait with `tensor_wait(1)` (i.e. s_wait_tensorcnt 0x2 when counting both tensors) at the top of iteration i+1, never 0 inside the loop. The prologue issues iterations 0 and 1.
(4) Delete the staging stores (L381-395) and the `pre[4+...]` Q/dO fragments. For hh in 2 and dt in NDT: `qa = ds_load_b128(ringQ + (hh*16+row)*272 + half*16 + dt*64)` and `(+32)`, shuffled into v16. dO the same. Write the loads for hh=1 in source before the hh=0 softmax VALU, so the loads are one phase ahead as in ASM section 7.
(5) The tr16 b_do/b_q addresses now point into ring slot i%2. Load them per dtile just before use in the dV loop (double-buffered), not all 8 up front.
(6) The masked loop (carry=False) issues its own TDM plus tensor_wait(0). It runs 4 iterations/WG, so the cost does not matter.
(7) Remove the `rocdl.sched_barrier(0)` in _ldqd (no b128 VMEM left to order).
Gate: toy launch first, in a separate process with the flock per gfx1250-card-safety (a wrong TDM extent waits on a tensorcnt that never retires and hangs the card; tdm_screen.py:1-2). Then ISA: 0 buffer_load_b128 in the loop, 0 v_mov_b64, 2 TDM + 8 vec4 per iteration, and every s_wait_tensorcnt non-zero.
evidence: dkdv ATT classes this removes, per iteration of 1715: VMEM prefetch issue phase D 100.5 (WALL:111); rotation v_mov_b64 + WAR v_nop phase M 192.5 (WALL:410-548); mid-body Q/dO stores + switches C/E/F about 161 (WALL:54,112,116,151,157); the 16 delayed hh=1 stores inside the phase-K drain (about 60 at 3-4.6 cycles/op); and part of the address/loop VALU B (53). That is about 560 cycles. It adds 32 ds_load_b128 (about 50-80 issue, hidden if one phase ahead) and a tensor wait, which ASM pays 125-227 cycles per 80-WMMA step (asm report section 9), about 100-150 cycles here. Net about 350-400 cycles, about 20-23% of k_dkdv. Discounted, because ku2 (0 v_mov_b64) measured +7.3% on B0 (lab-kdq REPORT.md:30) and cycle attributions have not translated one to one: expect about 12% of k_dkdv, about 8% of bwd on top of dkdv_flip. The same ASM data path runs with 0 buffer_load in its loop (asm report section 4).
vgpr_risk: VGPR goes down, which is the point. Removing 128 carried Q/dO + 128 held Q/dO fragments + 64 bulk tr16 operands, and streaming about 32+32 instead, should give about 760 -> about 480-560. The resident set is acc 256 + K/V fragments 128 = 384. Report the exact number; it decides dkdv_flip_tdm_2w.
bounds_risk: New: TDM descriptors. The tile origin (bat*Sq + qt*32, qh*D) must lie fully inside (B*Sq, Hq*D) for every issued prefetch, including the clamped last-iteration prefetch (_clampqt / the jj clamp at L535). A descriptor extent error hangs rather than faults. The CPU proof must enumerate every TDM issue (prologue 2, loop i+2, masked loop) on all shapes and show row+32 <= B*Sq and col+128 <= Hq*D. LDS ring offsets are static.
closed_axis_conflict: #34 TDM (CR/CM, h47-49, g56) was closed because the 32 buffer_load_b128 were dual-use (they fed both LDS and the S-GEMM registers), so TDM removed nothing. After dkdv_flip plus reading the S operand from LDS, the staging is no longer dual-use, which removes h49's premise. #34 explicitly lists this as O 'only as part of an aiter-style redesign where the GEMM reads B from LDS'. It also differs from #13 (P1 deleted the Q/dO LDS path, -6.98%): here the LDS path stays and the global->VGPR->LDS copy goes. Not g56: LSE/delta stay on VMEM.

name: dkdv_flip_tdm_2w
idea: Use the VGPR diet from dkdv_flip_tdm to run 2 one-wave k_dkdv workgroups per SIMD: VGPR <= 512 and LDS <= 40 KB per WG, so 8 WGs/CU. There are no barriers and no change to BLOCK_KV or Q/dO traffic; each WG still owns 32 kv rows, so unlike o1/g4o no operand stream doubles. The second wave hides the 29-cycle WMMA<->DS switches, the tensor waits and the unhidden VALU runs of the first. The roofline report measured that only a second wave on the SIMD hides these.
change_spec:
Copy arms/dkdv_flip_tdm to arms/dkdv_flip_tdm_2w.
(1) LDS: drop the 64 KB segment split (LDS_SEG, L246-252; g39 was null) and allocate exactly ring 34816 B, or less. The epilogue no longer uses LDS after dkdv_flip.
(2) VGPR <= 512. Pass no waves_per_eu/maxnreg (closed #15: -32%/-5x). The budget must come from the code shape: acc 256 + K/V fragments 128 + S/dP acc 32 + P/dS bf16 32 + streamed A operands 2x16 + LSE/delta 32 (+16 carried) + about 30 scalars/addresses, about 540. If the compile gate shows > 512 with 0 spill:
  (a) process LSE/delta per hh (load hh=1's vec4 after hh=0's softmax, -16);
  (b) move V to an LDS image (32x272 = 8704 B, written once in the prologue from vf, the same idiom as FUSED5's lds_k at lab3/f5/kernels.py:345-358), and read vf[kh][dt] with 2 ds_load_b128 per use in the dP GEMM (-64 VGPR, +16 ds_load per iteration). LDS then totals 43.5 KB, so shrink the ring rows to 264 B (pad 8) to get 34.8 -> 33.8 + 8.7 = 42.5 KB. If that is still > 40 KB, TDM depth 1.5: the dO slot is double-buffered, Q single, and Q is issued after the dK^T GEMM's last tr16.
(3) `@flyc.kernel(known_block_size=[32,1,1])` is unchanged. Occupancy follows from the resources alone. Check .vgpr_count <= 512 and the LDS size in 21_final_isa.s.
(4) Grid order: keep longest-first dispatch (g03/g40) so pairs of co-resident WGs have similar lengths.
Gate: compile gives vgpr_count <= 512, 0 spill, LDS <= 40960. PMC then shows about 2 waves per SIMD (SQ_WAVES / cycles), and ATT on CU1 shows two interleaved wave timelines on one SIMD.
evidence: 0930__roofline/REPORT.md: a WMMA->DS->WMMA switch costs about 29 cycles per wave and is 'hidden only by a second wave on the SIMD'; the per-iteration model puts about 800 cycles/iteration as hideable ($RF:143). After dkdv_tdm the remaining non-WMMA exposed time is about 1715 - 512 - 560 + 150 = about 790 cycles/iteration: switches, tensor waits, J-phase VALU 91, DS issue, SALU 123. With 2 waves the SIMD floor is WMMA 512 + non-co-issuable VALU (about 170) + SALU/DS issue share, about 800-900/iteration, versus about 1300 for 1 wave. That is -30% of k_dkdv in the ideal case. The discount for L2/TDM contention (ASM's slow waves are +70% under full-chip load, asm report section 13) halves it: about 15% of k_dkdv, about 10% of bwd.
vgpr_risk: High. 512 is tight against a resident 384 (acc 256 + K/V 128). This arm dies if the diet fails with 0 spill; the V-in-LDS fallback trades 64 VGPR for 16 ds_load_b128 per iteration. Never use maxnreg to force it.
bounds_risk: No new global index beyond dkdv_flip_tdm. The only new address is the V LDS image in fallback (b) (static offsets). Re-run the dkdv_flip_tdm TDM proof unchanged.
closed_axis_conflict: #16 (k_dq at 2 waves/SIMD: o1 +14.7%, g4o +13.5%) was closed for k_dq because BQ=32 without prefetch doubled K/V traffic; #16 is marked RE for the mechanism, and 'a form with shared K/V was never tried'. This form keeps every stream identical (BLOCK_KV 32, one WG per kv tile) and relies on TDM for the prefetch. #14/g55/g14 (single-wave occupancy, BLOCK_KV) were 1 wave/SIMD. #17 w4 also ran 1 wave/SIMD, so switch hiding was never tested (history item 17). #15 is avoided by not using waves_per_eu/maxnreg.

name: w4_tdm_share
idea: Stepping stone to the fused 5-GEMM kernel, and a barrier-cost gate. Build a 4-wave, BLOCK_KV=128 k_dkdv (wave w owns kv[32w, 32w+32) with its own K/V fragments and dK/dV accumulators, exactly the per-wave body of dkdv_flip_tdm). The 4 waves share one TDM-loaded Q/dO ring per WG, so global Q/dO traffic and TDM issue drop 4x. The waves sync with bare split barriers placed the ASM way, not with fx.barrier(). No dQ yet.
change_spec:
Copy arms/dkdv_flip_tdm to arms/w4_tdm_share.
(1) Launch `block=(128,1,1)` (`known_block_size=[128,1,1]`), BLOCK_KV=128, grid.y = Skv/128. Add `wave = fx.Int32(fx.thread_idx.x) // 32` and `lane = thread_idx.x % 32` (h58 prerequisite: lane_id plus an independent wave variable). kv0 = bid*128 + wave*32. Per-wave K/V fragments, acc and the causal mask use this kv0. The q loop start qp_start is computed from the WG's first kv row (bid*128), and waves whose kv range is fully masked for a q pair still execute it (the masked path zeroes P). Keep the mask/full split using the WG-level bounds: nmaskp becomes 4 pairs.
(2) Wave 0 alone issues the TDM for Q and dO (2 per iteration, `if wave == 0` via a scalar branch, as ASM's single issuing wave per WG step). The ring is 3-deep (3 x 17408 = 52 KB) so the issue can run 2 iterations ahead.
(3) Per iteration, using `from flydsl._mlir.dialects import rocdl as r; r.s_barrier_signal(-1)` / `r.s_barrier_wait(-1)` with NO fence (BARRIER-CENSUS F1: fx.barrier() = fence release + signal + wait + fence acquire, which produced the s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0 drain of 36 VMEM + 40 stores):
  BS1 at loop head, after `tensor_wait` for slot i (wave 0; other waves have nothing to wait on), then BW1 after the first 3 S/dP WMMAs (the ring slot is valid only after BW1).
  BS2 after this wave's last tr16 read of slot i-1 (end of the dK^T GEMM of the previous iteration, i.e. the WAR guard), then BW2 before wave 0 re-issues TDM into that slot, with at least 6 WMMAs between them.
  Waits are explicit partial `s_wait_dscnt` via rocdl intrinsics, never 0.
(4) The LSE/delta vec4 loads stay per wave (each wave needs all 32 q; 8 b128, small).
(5) Epilogue per wave as in dkdv_flip. LDS 52 KB + 0, VGPR as dkdv_flip_tdm (~500-560), so 1 wave/SIMD and 1 WG/CU-quarter, the same as ASM.
(6) impl.py: grid (Hkv, Skv/128, B), longest-first. Add near/far pairing (WG takes kv blocks j and 63-j, as ASM does; ASMcsv:3628 outer loop hit=2/wave) to balance the causal triangle.
Gate: ISA per barrier region must show no loadcnt/dscnt 0x0 before any s_barrier_signal, and 3-6 WMMAs between each signal and its wait (census method of BARRIER-CENSUS.md). ATT: barrier stall <= 15% of step cycles (ASM: 208 of 1581, about 13%).
evidence: ASM report section 6: 2 split barriers per step cost 208 cycles/step (13%, 154-261). ASM does it with symmetric work, waits placed before the signal, and 3-6 WMMAs between signal and wait. Our w4 lost 0.664x (bwd-history section 5) with barrier-1 forcing `s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0` over 36 VMEM prefetches and 40 stores and only 1 WMMA in R1 (BARRIER-CENSUS.md table, w4 row); s2 proved bare intrinsics emit no drain. The gain in its own right: Q/dO global/L2 traffic falls 4x (about 69 GB -> 17 GB at prod; the per-WG estimate is 8.4 MB x 8192 WGs) and TDM issue per wave falls 4x. Net of the 208-cycle barrier cost, expect about 0-3% of bwd versus dkdv_flip_tdm. This arm is mainly the go/no-go measurement for w4_fused_dq.
vgpr_risk: Same as dkdv_flip_tdm (~500-560). The WG is 4 waves x 1/SIMD, so no occupancy rung is at stake. Watch for LLVM hoisting per-wave constants into more SGPR/VGPR.
bounds_risk: New index expressions: kv0 = bid*128 + wave*32; the Skv%128 remainder must be predicated (masked kv rows -> P=0, store predicated) with no tail loop; the TDM tile origin as in dkdv_flip_tdm; the pairing index 63-j. The CPU proof must show every (b, qh, q pair, kv row) is visited exactly once across waves and pairs (extend lab3/bounds_proof.py, which already checks exactly-once for BLOCK_KV=32) and that TDM extents are true on prod, proxy, fast and UT shapes.
closed_axis_conflict: #17/#18 (4-wave BLOCK_KV=128: w4 0.664x, X1 0.804, X2 0.872, nobar 0.923; h51's 0.95x ceiling; the h53/h54 'no fifth armchair mechanism' rule). This is a pre-registered experiment with an ISA census gate, not a new mechanism. It differs in 3 measured ways: (a) no VMEM prefetch in flight across barriers (TDM/tensorcnt), which removes the 36-load forced drain; (b) bare signal/wait with no fence (F1); (c) the flip removes the P/dS LDS phase, so the region between barriers holds WMMAs, not 40 tr16 loads with 1 WMMA. h51's 0.95 ceiling was measured on the old staging design, and its 'barrier-free but wrong' build still carried the dual-use VMEM staging.

name: w4_fused_dq
idea: The 5-GEMM structure, done the ASM way on top of w4_tdm_share. Each wave also computes a 32q x 32d dQ slice (d split by wave) = dS[32q x 128kv] * K[128kv x 32d]. dS is exchanged through LDS (each wave writes its own 32 kv columns and all 4 read all 128). The K slice for dQ stays resident in 64 VGPR. dQ is deferred one step, scaled, and scattered with 32 fp32 SCOPE_DEV atomics per wave per step, one per WMMA gap. This deletes k_dqg (35% of bwd cycles) and its S/dP recompute, i.e. 2 of our 7 GEMMs; an fp32->bf16 convert kernel is added.
change_spec:
Copy arms/w4_tdm_share to arms/w4_fused_dq.
(1) Prologue, once per WG: write K[128x128] to an LDS image (the FUSED5 idiom, lab3/f5/kernels.py:345-358, per wave for its 32 rows, then one barrier). Each wave tr16-loads its resident dQ B-operand `kq[kc][dsub]` = K[kc*32:(kc+1)*32, wave*32 + dsub*16 : +16] for kc in 4 and dsub in 2: 8 fragments x 8 VGPR = 64. The K image region can then be reused.
(2) dS exchange: after dS bf16 for both hh is formed (dkdv_flip step 4), each wave stores its dS[32q x 32kv] row-major to `lds_ds_x[slot][q][wave*32 + kv]` (row = 128 kv x 2 B + 16 pad = 272 B; 4 ds_store_b128 per wave, ASM phase 4 uses 4). Slot = i%2 (double-buffered). The step's existing BS2/BW2 pair orders it: the store happens before BS2, and the reads come after BW2 of the next step.
(3) dQ GEMM for step i-1 (deferred), placed in the source between the dK^T GEMM and the next S GEMM: for qh in 2 and dsub in 2, 4 chained WMMAs over kc with A = dS fragment read by ds_load_b128 from lds_ds_x[(i-1)%2] (row = qh*16 + row, cols kc*32 + half*8 and +16) and B = kq[kc][dsub], starting from zero. That is 16 WMMAs, 32 VGPR of dQ acc. Then multiply by scale.
(4) Atomics: dq_acc fp32 [B,Sq,Hq,D] is a plain global view `fx.Tensor(fx.make_view(fx.get_iter(DQA), fx.make_layout((1<<30,1),(1,1))))` with `fx.make_copy_atom(fx.UniversalAtomicAdd(fx.Float32, rocdl.SyncScope.Agent), fx.Float32)` (lab3/f5/kernels.py:285-292; BufferAtomicAdd emits SCOPE_CU, h42). Per wave per step there are 32 atomics: element (q = q0' + qh*16 + half*8 + si, d = wave*32 + dsub*16 + row). Compute ONE base address VGPR per (qh, half) at iteration start and express si and dsub as compile-time byte offsets (si*Hq*D*4, dsub*64) so the backend folds them into the immediate `offset:` (FUSED5 rebuilt 8 address VGPRs and paid 162 s_wait_xcnt). In the source, emit the 32 atomics of step i-1 ONE AFTER EACH WMMA of the step-i dV^T/dK^T GEMMs (32 WMMAs, a 1:1 interleave, as ASM spreads them over phases 6 and 2-3). Never add a storecnt wait.
(5) WMMA per wave per step = S 8 + dP 8 + dV 16 + dK 16 + dQ 16 = 64 per 32q x 32kv per wave, versus 64 + k_dqg's 48 today.
(6) impl.py: `dq_acc = torch.zeros(b,sq,hq,d, fp32)`; launch w4 k_dkdv_fused; then `launch_redsp_q(dq_acc, dq_o, n_vec, nsp=1)` (kernels.py:1558-1597 already converts fp32->bf16 for nsp=1). Remove the k_dqg launch. k_delta is unchanged.
(7) Stage gates, in order: (A) ATOM=0 (dQ WMMA computed and discarded via a sink store once per WG) against w4_tdm_share; the extra time must be <= 20% (the 16 WMMAs are +25% of matrix work, and FUSED5 P1 paid +30% only because of the 32 extra tr16 per iteration). (B) ATOM=1. Before B, run P2's KVG=4 atomic probe on A0 (lab3/atomprobe, 2.46 ms on B0). Go if T_op < r29.
evidence: PMC: k_dqg = 4.00e6 of 11.44e6 cycles/SIMD (35%). Per 32q x 32kv unit, fly = 2738 PMC (dkdv 1766 + dqg 973) versus ASM 1853 (asm report section 10). ASM's cost of fusing, per step: +128 cycles for 16 WMMAs, atomics 430 (208-634), barriers 208. Built on w4_tdm_share (k_dkdv about 1250/unit): 1250 + 128 + 430 + ~70 (the barrier increment over w4_tdm_share) = about 1880, versus 1250 + 973 = 2223, a -15% op gain. With atomics at the fast-wave cost (208) it is about -25%; with the slow cost (634), about -6%. Atomic payload drops to aiter's 17.45 GB (a 4x smaller payload than FUSED5's 69 GB; P2 KVG=4 alone = 2.46 ms on B0). Expect about 12% of bwd beyond w4_tdm_share. This is the only arm that can take fly below ASM (ASM 5.503 ms).
vgpr_risk: Moderate to high. Per wave: acc 256 + K,V fragments for S/dP 128 + dQ K slice 64 = 448 resident (the same as ASM, asm report section 4), plus S/dP acc 32, P/dS bf16 32, dQ acc 32, streamed A operands about 48, LSE/delta 32, and about 40 addresses: about 670-760 of 1024, at 1 wave/SIMD like ASM (.vgpr_count 1024, AITER-5GEMM-STUDY.md:43). f5-res (1024, 29 spills) is not comparable because it kept all of K^T (128 d) resident at BLOCK_KV=32; here each wave keeps only a 32-d slice.
bounds_risk: High. New index expressions: the atomic address (b, q, qh_head, d) including the causal-edge q rows. Atomics must be predicated off for q >= Sq, never clamped (a clamped atomic corrupts a live row). The dS exchange offsets are static. Prove on CPU that each dq element receives exactly the causally valid (kv block) contributions, that max index = B*Sq*Hq*D-1, and that deferral flushes the final step's dQ after the loop (the epilogue must issue the last step's GEMM and atomics). The dq_acc zero plus convert covers the whole tensor (NaN-poison coverage gate). dk/dv stay bitwise run to run (atomics touch only dq); dq's run-to-run gate is >= 70 dB (FUSED5 measured 93-98 dB at a 4x larger count).
closed_axis_conflict:
#25 FUSED5 (0.391x) and #27 (deterministic fusion). This arm is non-deterministic dq, allowed since the 09-25 contract change. Why FUSED5 lost, and what differs, from its own files:
(1) Payload and density: BLOCK_KV=32 gave 128 atomics per 64 WMMAs (2.0/WMMA, 69 GB); here it is 32 per 64 WMMAs per wave (0.5/WMMA; ASM 0.4), 17.45 GB.
(2) Placement: FUSED5 issued them as two 64-deep s_clause bursts immediately after the dQ WMMA, on 8 rebuilt address VGPRs, producing 162 s_wait_xcnt (FUSED5-RESULT section 3). The atomic cost was 14.6 ms, 3.3x its standalone 4.43 ms. Here: deferred one step, 1:1 interleaved with WMMAs, immediate offsets, no xcnt/storecnt waits.
(3) dQ B operand: FUSED5 re-read K^T with 32 tr16 per iteration, which is why P1 was +30% (1095 instructions/body). Here the K slice is resident.
(4) The history note 'ASM hides atomics with 4 waves' is inaccurate. ASM is also 1 wave/SIMD (1 WG of 4 waves per CU, asm report section 1). It hides atomics by distribution and still pays 27% for them.
FUSED5's 4-wave gate (x <= 7.6%) was computed against a +30% P1 that included the tr16 reload. Stage A re-measures that x in this form. The barrier axis (#17) is gated by w4_tdm_share first.

That selects the `elif DQ_PF:` kvloop_full at kernels.py:~1382 and the matching prologue branch at ~1433 (`out = kvloop_full(init + _ldkv(0), nfull)`). Predicted op time = 4.255 + 2.214 = 6.469 vs r29's 6.544, i.e. −1.15%. The U2 ATT (dispatch_11 csv:670) shows the tail-clump prefetch gets only 214-490 cycles of lead. That is a U2-specific cost, which fits the reversal.
vgpr_risk: None. This is the r19h k_dqg configuration, which already shipped and passed the gates.
bounds_risk: None. Same index expressions (r19h path, jj clamp at kernels.py:~1388).
closed_axis_conflict: History #22 (u2n/h70) is marked RE: it won on B0 (−3.06%) but loses on reflashed A0. This arm is the A0 re-measurement that #22 asks for. It is not a new lever.

name: dqg_tailpf
idea: Keep U2, but issue body 2's K/V prefetch (the 'tail clump', block ii+2) inside body 1, right after body 1's last S/dP use of the carried set. It stays a single clump, only earlier. Today LLVM sinks it to the very end of the trip (cum ~2890-3314 of 3350), so the next trip's `s_wait_loadcnt 0x20` gets only 214-490 cycles of lead. That wait is the whole k_dqg loadcnt stall, and it also drives the slow-wave VMEM excess.
change_spec:
Base: copy of r29, so DQ_U2 stays True.
1) Add a keyword to `_body` (kernels.py:1277): `def _body(acc, pre, kv0, do_mask, kv0_n, carry=True, pf_mid=None, take_nxt=None)`.
   - When `take_nxt` is a list (body 2 in U2), skip `nxt = _ldkv(kv0_n)` at 1279 and use `nxt = take_nxt`.
   - When `pf_mid` is a kv0 value (body 1 in U2), issue the second prefetch inside the kt loop at 1284.
2) Variant a (whole clump). After the `for kt` loop ends (just before `a_ds = ...` at 1335), add `nxt2 = _ldkv(pf_mid)` followed by `rocdl.sched_barrier(0x78F)`. Mask 0x78F lets everything except VMEM (0x10/0x20/0x40) cross, so only the loads are pinned. Return `new + nxt + nxt2`.
3) Variant b (split by kt, even earlier). Add `_ldkv_kt(kv0, kt)` (the kt slice of `_ldkv`, 16 loads). Emit it for kt=0 right after the kt=0 S/dP WMMA loop and softmax. At that point carried pre[0:16] is dead: K is stored to LDS and the kfr/vfr WMMAs are issued. Emit kt=1 after the kt=1 block. Put the same 0x78F fence after each.
4) In the U2 `kvloop_full` (kernels.py:1365-1380):
   - Replace the two `_body` calls with `mid = _body(st_acc, st_pre, ii*KV, False, (ii+1)*KV, pf_mid=jj*KV)`.
   - `mid` returns acc + nxt(ii+1) + nxt2(jj).
   - Then `final = yield _body(mid_acc, mid_nxt, (ii+1)*KV, False, None, take_nxt=mid_nxt2)`.
   - Keep the jj clamp exactly as in the current code.
Gate:
   - compile ≤1024 VGPR, 0 spill/scratch;
   - in 21_final_isa.s the 32 loads of block ii+2 must sit before body 2's first S/dP WMMA;
   - count WMMAs between the last of those loads and the loop-head `s_wait_loadcnt 0x20`: need ≥ ~100 WMMA, i.e. more than 1000 cycles of lead.
Then run arm.sh. If fast, take an ATT (att-target-cu 1) and check that the loadcnt 0x20 stall drops from 204/trip.
vgpr_risk: Medium. The design intent keeps lifetimes the same: in variant a, nxt2 is born after the carried set (128 VGPR) dies. If LLVM does not reuse those registers, k_dqg (991 today) would pass 1024 and spill, which fails the gate. Variant b has the lowest pressure because each half is born exactly when its 64-VGPR half dies.
bounds_risk: None for the addresses: `_ldkv(jj*KV_STEP)` keeps the same clamped jj and the same gfrag2 expressions, only its position moves. Results are bitwise identical because the loaded values do not change. Still re-run the CPU clamp proof for jj < 2n.
closed_axis_conflict: This is not g63 (prefetch depth 2, −19.33%, history #4): depth stays 1. It is not g66's load spreading (−21.93%, #5; h37 +22%): the clump stays contiguous. The 0x78F fence only pins VMEM order, and a mask fence of this kind already ships in the champion (k_dkdv g51 sched_barrier(0) at kernels.py:300). That makes it different from the closed full-region clamps and group barriers (#8, 'sched_barrier between bodies +16-21%'). History #9 notes LLVM ignores soft hints, which is why the ISA gate checks placement before any card time.

name: mem_soffset
idea: Move the uniform part of every loop buffer_load address (batch/head base plus the loop-varying kv0 or q-tile row offset) into the SGPR soffset operand. Keep one loop-invariant per-lane voffset, and put the dt/u column offsets in the instruction immediate. Today the loop recomputes VGPR addresses with v_or/v_mad/v_add_lshl and the loads use `null` soffset (csv:643 `buffer_load_b128 v[2:5], v90, s[76:79], null offen`). In k_dqg the recycled address VGPRs cause the three s_wait_xcnt stalls. In k_dkdv they cause the VALU→VMEM dependency gaps plus phase B address math.
change_spec:
Use flydsl 0.3.2 raw intrinsics: `fx.rocdl.get_buffer_rsrc(ptr)` (flydsl/expr/rocdl/universal.py:~300) and `rocdl.raw_ptr_buffer_load(res, rsrc, offset, soffset)` (flydsl/expr/rocdl/__init__.py:791).

k_dqg (_dqg_impl):
- After `g_k`/`g_v` at kernels.py:~1206 add `rs_k = fx.rocdl.get_buffer_rsrc(fx.get_iter(g_k))`, and the same for V.
- Precompute once, outside the loops: `vo = ((row * rs_kv) + half) * 16` (bytes, per lane, loop-invariant).
- Replace `gfrag2` (1230-1233) as used by `_ldkv` (1268-1275) with:
  `sb = fx.Int32(rocdl.readfirstlane(i32, ((base_kv + r*rs_kv) * 16).ir_value()))`, where r = kv0 + kt*16 is uniform;
  `a = raw_ptr_buffer_load(v8bf16, rs_k, vo + fx.Int32(dt*64), sb)`;
  `b = raw_ptr_buffer_load(v8bf16, rs_k, vo + fx.Int32(dt*64 + 32), sb)`.
  The constants must be the outermost add so ISel folds them into `offset:`. Keep the qf/dof/prologue gfrag unchanged.

k_dkdv:
- In `_ldqd` (kernels.py:273-310) do the same for Q/dO: `sb = readfirstlane((base_q + (q0 + hh*16)*rs_q)*16)`, `vo_q = (row*rs_q + half)*16` hoisted out of the loop, imm = dt*64 + u*32.
- For the 4 LSE/delta b32 loads: `sb = readfirstlane((base_l + q0 + hh*16)*4)`, `vo_l = row*4`.
- Keep `rocdl.sched_barrier(0)` at 300 exactly where it is.

Gate (ISA):
- in both loops the buffer_loads show an SGPR soffset and `offset:` immediates;
- no `v_or_b32 vN, 0xc0/0xe0` and no s_wait_xcnt in the k_dqg loop (Vaddr 11128-11152 today);
- k_dkdv phase-B VALU count drops;
- VGPR ≤ r29 (729/991), 0 spill.

Ship the k_dqg half and the k_dkdv half as sub-arms mem_soffset_q and mem_soffset_kv so each can be A/B'd.
vgpr_risk: Low, likely negative: fewer address VGPRs are live, and the per-lane voffset becomes one loop-invariant VGPR per buffer. It does add a few SGPRs (readfirstlane results), and SGPR pressure is not an issue.
bounds_risk: High attention needed. Every load index is rewritten as soff + voff + imm, and a CPU proof must show byte-exact equality with the old t*16 (or idx*4) for every lane, dt, u and loop index. On gfx12-class raw buffers soffset may be excluded from the num_records range check. In k_dkdv, where descriptors carry TRUE extents (r1.i7.g07, h33 clamp), prove that every clamped (qt_n, gh_n) address is in bounds without relying on the descriptor. Also assert in impl.py that tensor bytes < 2^31: prod K is 64 MB, so this is fine. k_dqg's fake 1<<30 descriptors stay as they are (bwd-history rule: do not 'fix' them). Masked loops keep the old path.
closed_axis_conflict: Resembles g92 (constant hoist, 0.9662, history #21) and ku2's 'fewer issued instructions'. The difference: g92 hoisted VALU constants into registers, which raised pressure. This arm moves address math onto SGPR/immediate operands and removes the xcnt dependency (a TA register-recycle stall), which no earlier arm touched. The xcnt stall evidence is new (reflashed-A0 ATT).

name: dkdv_lse_late
idea: Remove k_dkdv's single biggest global-load stall: `s_wait_loadcnt 0x23` before the loop-carried copy `v_mov v650 <- v693`. This is lse for hh=0 of the NEXT iteration. The scheduler places the copy right after V650's last use, about 464 cycles after the b32 load issued, so 29% of iterations wait ~434 cycles. The fix is to load lse0 for iteration i+1 directly into the carried register after its last use in iteration i. With no copy there is no early wait, and the load's first real wait becomes the loop-tail `s_wait_loadcnt 0x0` about 2300 cycles later.
vgpr_risk: Low. The carried tuple shape is unchanged, and if coalescing succeeds one staging VGPR (v693) is freed. Worst case, if RA does not coalesce, the ISA is the same as r29 and the gate rejects the arm at zero card cost.
bounds_risk: The lse address is the same expression with clamped (qt_n, gh_n) from qloop_full's jj clamp, plus z. z is 0 whenever the anchor's bits are non-negative. exp2 gives +0 or a positive value, and a NaN with the sign bit set would give a negative offset. That can only happen if the inputs are already NaN, and it is then caught by the descriptor's true extent (returns 0), with no memory hazard. Include this in the CPU proof note.
closed_axis_conflict: This belongs to the g27 / g48 / g51 LSE-prefetch family, and g27 died at −14.6% when the consuming wait turned into a full drain. The difference: prefetch depth and FIFO head position stay the same for del0, lse1 and del1. Only lse0's issue point moves, to where its register is free, and its first covering wait is the existing tail loadcnt 0x0, which already drains everything. That means no new partial→full drain is created. Evidence that it is open: the reflashed-A0 ATT shows the copy placement as the cause, which the B0 rounds never observed.

name: dqg_dkdv_streams
idea: Run k_dqg on a second HIP stream concurrently with k_dkdv after k_delta. The two kernels are independent: both read q/k/v/do/lse/delta, and they write disjoint outputs. Running them together removes the k_dkdv→k_dqg serialization point (k_dkdv's drain tail with a partly idle machine, then k_dqg's ramp). The dispatcher can then fill SIMDs freed by finished k_dkdv WGs with k_dqg WGs. It is also the only way to overlap two kernels with different bottlenecks on one CU: k_dkdv is DS/LDS bound, k_dqg is VMEM/VALU bound.
evidence:
Prod grids:
- k_dkdv: 8192 one-wave WGs on 1024 slots (8 dispatch waves), longest-first, impl.py:168-176;
- k_dqg: 16384 WGs, descending bid (kernels.py:1196).
Op time 6.544 ms (kbench) vs k_dq 2.290 + rest 4.255 means the kernels already run back to back. Each kernel's last dispatch wave leaves SIMDs idle while the longest WGs finish; with longest-first ordering this tail is typically 1-3% per kernel. The two kernels have different pressure profiles:
- k_dqg DS traffic is ~9 B/clk (dqg report §5), and its losses are VMEM/VALU;
- k_dkdv's losses are DS drain and switches (dkdv report §1b).
Co-residency on one CU across SIMDs therefore does not contend for the same unit. Estimate 0.5-1.5% of bwd from removing one drain+ramp and tail overlap.
vgpr_risk: None, because the kernels are unchanged. Occupancy is still 1 wave per SIMD for each kernel. LDS per CU: at most 4 × 70656 (k_dkdv) = 282 KB < 320 KB, so there is enough room when a CU mixes k_dkdv WGs with k_dqg WGs (8704 B each).
bounds_risk: None for indices. Correctness risk is only stream ordering: every input consumed by s2 must be produced before `s2.wait_stream(stream)`, which is true after k_delta. The outputs must be joined before return. dk/dv bitwise determinism is unaffected (disjoint outputs, no atomics). Run the 200-run bitwise gate anyway, because scheduling changes.
closed_axis_conflict: Not covered by any closed axis. g03/g40 (longest-first dispatch, history #39) and split-K (#32/#33) addressed tails inside a kernel, not across kernels. #35 (delta fusion) is a different lever and is capped at 1.6%.

name: dqg_tdm_kvlds
idea: Aiter-style memory path for k_dqg. TDM (tensor DMA) loads the K and V tiles for block ii+1 directly into a double-buffered LDS ring, one or two instructions per block. S/dP read their A operands (K and V fragments) with ds_load_b128 from LDS, and dQ keeps reading K^T with ds_load_tr16 from the same K tile. This removes all 64 loop buffer_load_b128, the 32 ds_store_b128 of K, the xcnt/loadcnt/VMEM issue stalls and the 256-VGPR K/V prefetch sets.
vgpr_risk: Low: it frees about 256 VGPR (two 128-VGPR K/V prefetch sets). It does not reach 512, so no 2-wave occupancy.
bounds_risk: New index space. The TDM descriptor extents must be the TRUE K/V extents (rows = b*Skv, strided by head). A CPU proof must show that every tile start (kv0 = clamp(ii+1)) is inside [0, Skv−32] for the head, so the tile never crosses into another head. Keep the masked loop on the old buffer path. Card safety: gfx1250-card-safety lists two TDM wedge paths, so run the toy first and alone, with the flock and dmesg classification of tools/run.sh.
closed_axis_conflict: History #34 (TDM, h23/h47-49/g56) is closed only 'for the current design, because the buffer loads feed both LDS and the register operands (g09)'. The row explicitly leaves it Open for a redesign in which the GEMM reads its operand from LDS. This arm is that redesign for k_dqg, where the dual use (K → LDS for dQ, K/V → VGPR for S/dP) is removed by reading S/dP operands from LDS. g56 (async LSE/delta to LDS, −6.84%) was a different, tiny load.
